text:
For a **multi-day hurricane outage**, I’d choose the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W solar-panel kit**. Its 2,073.6 Wh battery is a better fit for keeping essentials like a fridge and CPAP going than a smaller 1 kWh unit. The kit is listed at [$1,199](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit); see the [kit details](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-hurricane-season).

One caveat: **200 W of solar is modest**, and cloudy storm conditions can slow recharging substantially. If you can, budget for more panel capacity, and don’t count on solar alone during the storm.

If you mainly need to charge phones, lights, and a router—and want to spend less—the **Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200 W panel** is a smaller option; it has a 1,070 Wh battery and 1,500 W output ([kit comparison](https://www.preparedstates.com/kit/solar-generators)). Actual runtime depends on what you plug in and how often.
